chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has imposed an obligation for the poor in the wealth of the rich — they will not be praised except by fulfilling it — and it is the zakat. By it their blood is protected, and by it they are named Muslims. But Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has imposed in the wealth of the rich rights other than zakat, for He (Mighty and Majestic) said:
'And those in whose wealth there is a known right' [70:24].

So the 'known right' is from other than the zakat, and it is something which the man imposes upon himself in his wealth. It is obligated upon him that he impose it upon himself according to his capacity and the extent of his wealth, and he pays what he imposed upon himself, if he wishes, every day, or if he wishes, every Friday, or if he wishes, every month.
And Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has also said: 'and lend to Allah a goodly loan' [57:18], and this is other than the zakat.
And Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has also said: 'and spend out of what We have given them secretly and openly' [14:31].

And al-ma'un (acts of kindness) as well: it is a loan one gives, a possession one lends, and an act of goodness one performs. And among what Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has also imposed in wealth other than zakat is His (Mighty and Majestic) saying:

And whoever fulfills what Allah has imposed upon him has discharged what was due from him, and has rendered gratitude for what Allah has blessed him with in his wealth, when he praises Him for what Allah has blessed him with therein — for the capacity He has favored him with over others — and for having granted him success in fulfilling what Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has imposed upon him, and aided him in it.

key_terms.الحق المعلوم: Al-haqq al-ma'lum — the 'known right', a self-determined voluntary financial obligation mentioned in Quran 70:24
key_terms.الزكاة: Zakat — the obligatory alms-tax, one of the pillars of Islam
key_terms.السعة: Al-sa'a — financial capacity, abundance of wealth
key_terms.الماعون: Al-ma'un — acts of practical kindness: lending money, lending possessions, performing good deeds

ai.seo_question: What financial obligations beyond zakat does Islam impose on the wealthy?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elaborates on the financial obligations imposed by Allah beyond the obligatory zakat. He explains that the 'known right' mentioned in the Quran (70:24) refers to a self-imposed charitable obligation that a wealthy person determines according to his own capacity — payable daily, weekly, or monthly — in addition to lending, sharing possessions, and maintaining family ties as commanded in the Quran. This teaching was delivered to Sama'a ibn Mihran, a trusted companion of the Imam, in the context of clarifying the full scope of Islamic financial obligations for the wealthy.
